newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Bomb blast kills two in Algeria-report.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast kills two in Algeria-report.

text.p: A bomb explosion killed a brother and cousin of a Moslem guerrilla in a town 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, the newspaper Liberte said on Wednesday.

The Tuesday attack was the second this year targeting the house of an unnamed member of the Islamic Salvation Army (AIS), one of several guerrilla factions fighting the Algerian government, Liberte said.
It blamed a rival guerrilla faction for the attacks.
The AIS and its Armed Islamic Group are locked in a turf war in which hundreds of guerrillas have been reportedly killed in the past three years.
The bomb that exploded on Tuesday in Sidi Moussa town killed the guerrilla's brother and cousin who had returned to the abandoned house for family belongings, the newspaper said.
The rebel's father and sister were killed in the earlier bombing, according to Liberte.

El Watan newspaper said five schoolgirls were killed on Sunday near Berrouaghia town in the province of Medea. More than 80 civilians have died in the area in the past three months, mostly in massacres authorities blame on Moslem guerrillas.
The latest deaths come as the country is gearing up for June 5 parliamentary elections in which radical Islamists are barred from fielding candidates.

Algeria has been without a parliament since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the Islamic Salvation Front took a commanding lead. About 60,000 people have died in the five years of violence.
